nodes.title: DNA double-helix model
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Watson and Crick proposed antiparallel helical chains with complementary A–T and G–C pairs, drawing on chemical constraints and others’ experimental work.
nodes.uncertainty: The paper explicitly treats the model as unproved. Donohue, Franklin, Gosling, Wilkins, other King’s workers and prior chemical researchers are not collapsed into sole-person credit.
nodes.date_basis: Proposed structural model in the manuscript signed 2 April 1953; date belongs to model proposal, not discovery of DNA.

nodes.title: Parallel-current attraction and repulsion
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Two parallel straight conductor sections, one counterweighted and movable, carry currents from two voltaic piles; same-direction currents attract and opposite-direction currents repel.
nodes.uncertainty: The available English translation is modern and unattributed. No modern mathematical force law or exact September demonstration day is ascribed to this node.
nodes.date_basis: Composite memoir read 2 October includes communications of 18 and 25 September; exact experimental day not recovered.

nodes.title: Switching induces a second current
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Separately insulated windings around an iron ring connect to a battery and a remote galvanometer. Making or breaking the battery circuit gives opposite transient responses; steady current gives no sustained deflection.
nodes.uncertainty: This is an experimental result, not the later mathematical flux law or an efficient power transformer. The report deliberately rearranged experiments for exposition.
nodes.date_basis: Museum dates successful ring experiment to 29 August 1831; First Series gives the experimental configuration.

nodes.title: Dielectric induction test proposed
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: A proposed experiment seeks a relation between dielectric polarization and electromagnetic force, testing assumptions that connect Helmholtz’s electrodynamics to Maxwell’s equations.
nodes.uncertainty: A research programme, not an observed effect. Attribution of the problem’s precise theoretical motivation is Hertz’s later reconstruction; the Academy’s original announcement was not retrieved.
nodes.date_basis: Hertz’s retrospective introduction dates the Berlin Academy prize problem to 1879.

nodes.title: Reflected electrical waves in air
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: A spark oscillator illuminates a metal reflecting wall; moving and turning a spark-gap loop detects spatial strengthening and weakening consistent with incident/reflected waves.
nodes.uncertainty: Qualitative reflection/wave behavior only. Hertz later rejected the reliability of the air-versus-wire velocity comparison because of room/resonance effects; no precise light-speed measurement is claimed.
nodes.date_basis: Follows the November 1887 dielectric work and is reported in the 1888 air-wave paper; this interval avoids equating publication year with an unverified exact performance date.

nodes.title: Current deflects a needle
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: A wire closing a galvanic circuit deflects a nearby suspended magnetic needle; moving the wire above/below reverses deflection; nonmagnetic needles provide controls.
nodes.uncertainty: The reported circular electrical-conflict explanation is historical. No claim that all magnetic phenomena or modern field theory were established in this experiment.
nodes.date_basis: Repeated observations reported by 21 July 1820; day of initial discovery is not assigned.

nodes.title: Fairchild 2N1613 planar transistor
nodes.anchor_rationale: Selected as a scoped candidate for independent review.
nodes.summary: Fairchild 2N1613, NPN diffused-silicon planar transistor; not all later 2N1613 manufacturers or variants.
nodes.uncertainty: April is an explicitly reported sale month; the first transaction day and any earlier limited pre-release offer were not independently established.
nodes.date_basis: IEEE historian reports Fairchild sold its first planar transistor, type 2N1613, in this month.

nodes.title: Fairchild Micrologic Type F flip-flop
nodes.anchor_rationale: Selected as a scoped candidate for independent review.
nodes.summary: Fairchild Micrologic Type F integrated flip-flop, 1961 introductory evaluation product; isolation process of earliest sold samples unconfirmed.
nodes.uncertainty: March 1961 applies to first reported commercial evaluation offer, not to every Micrologic family part or later junction-isolated production die. The earliest sold die and its isolation are not established.
nodes.date_basis: Introduced in March and contemporary 29/31 March reports identify paid evaluation sales and an offer.

nodes.title: Hōkūleʻa built
nodes.anchor_rationale: The selected event documents the positively evidenced nonmarket mission of this specific configuration; this is a scoped deployment, not an inferred sale.
nodes.summary: Double-hulled voyaging canoe with cold-molded plywood hulls covered in fiberglass, built for experimental voyaging.
nodes.uncertainty: Modern reconstruction; successful voyages cannot by themselves authenticate every ancient design or migration route. Practice under sail preceded the 1976 research voyage; the anchor is the documented intended project voyage, not a claim that no earlier use occurred.
nodes.date_basis: PVS voyage timeline gives the outbound departure from Honolua Bay.

nodes.title: Hōkūleʻa design study
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Kāne and Emory selected widely recorded canoe features as a hypothesis about earlier forms for an experimental vessel.
nodes.uncertainty: Widespread occurrence does not itself prove antiquity. The node records the investigators’ design inference, not its validation.
nodes.date_basis: Low’s participant interview account dates the design project’s start to early 1973; Kāne describes the reasoning retrospectively.

nodes.title: Majuro cross-swell observations
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Navigator-identified vessel rocking and directional wave measurements were consistent with bent incident swells; multiple wave trains limited field validation.
nodes.uncertainty: The buoy did not resolve claimed reflected signals or dilep. Model agreement at another island is not direct verification of all local cues.
nodes.date_basis: WAM’s participant interview places buoy deployments during the field year beginning in 2005 and culminating in the 2006 voyage; the research paper also states a June 2005–September 2006 fieldwork interval. Exact deployment days are not given.

nodes.title: Tiber boat mills
nodes.anchor_rationale: The selected event documents the positively evidenced nonmarket mission of this specific configuration; this is a scoped deployment, not an inferred sale.
nodes.summary: Customary mill machinery suspended between moored boats, driven by river current below a bridge.
nodes.uncertainty: Literary account; the exact bridge and claims of sufficient flour are not independently verified. Nonmarket is a configuration-specific inference, not evidence of no transactions or a claim about all boat mills.
nodes.date_basis: Procopius narrates the response at the beginning of the siege; Bury places this episode in 537.

nodes.title: Comparative microscope tests
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Dallinger compared Zeiss objectives and compensating eyepieces with his existing high-power lenses, including trials swapping in the new eyepieces; he and Mayall also recorded independent judgments on a supplied series.
regions: Europe — Britain; instruments from Jena and London
nodes.uncertainty: These were reported visual comparisons with selected test objects and high-quality existing lenses, not a modern standardized quantitative trial. Dallinger’s restricted conclusions must not be generalized to all apochromats.
nodes.date_basis: The tests followed the 1886 instrument introductions and preceded Dallinger’s address on 9 February 1887; exact individual test dates are not supplied.

nodes.title: Briggs common logarithms
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Published common-logarithm tables following discussion and revision of Napier's scheme; the node is the 1617 publication, not sole attribution of the idea.
nodes.uncertainty: Briggs credited Napier for the useful normalization; the concept and numerical labour should not be assigned to a single inventor.
nodes.date_basis: Publication of Logarithmorum Chilias Prima in London after the 1615–1616 discussions with Napier.

nodes.title: Jupiter satellites tracked
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Repeated telescopic positions of objects near Jupiter, interpreted as four bodies revolving around it rather than fixed stars.
nodes.uncertainty: Priority disputes with other observers are not resolved here; the result alone does not distinguish every geocentric, geoheliocentric and heliocentric system.
nodes.date_basis: Dated observations begin 7 January; four objects are recorded on 13 January; interpretation follows the changing positions.

nodes.title: Lunar relief observed
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Repeated telescopic views of the lunar light-shadow boundary and isolated illuminated features interpreted as an uneven surface with elevations and depressions.
nodes.uncertainty: This is Galileo's observation programme, not the first human telescopic look at the Moon; the inference is distinct from a direct topographic survey.
nodes.date_basis: Museo Galileo dates the surviving Moon drawings to November–December 1609; the interpretation was published in 1610.

nodes.title: Ibn al-Banna arithmetic rules
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Condensed Book on the Operations of Arithmetic gives rules for known and unknown quantities, including place-aligned addition, without worked numerical examples.
nodes.uncertainty: No invention claim for the rules. Dating is a terminus before 1301; the wide interval encodes limited evidence rather than continuous development over the author's life.
nodes.date_basis: The critical edition says shortly before 1301; 1256 is the author's birth and only a conservative lower bound. The anchor near 1300 is approximate, not an attested composition year.

nodes.title: Napier logarithms
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Published logarithmic calculation and tables, in Napier's original normalization rather than modern base-10 form.
nodes.uncertainty: No universal priority asserted; independent logarithmic developments are outside the current scope.
nodes.date_basis: Publication of Mirifici logarithmorum canonis descriptio; not the beginning of Napier's decades of work.

nodes.title: Differential refraction experiments
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Prism investigations leading Newton to identify differing refrangibility among components of sunlight and to diagnose a limitation of simple refracting objectives.
nodes.uncertainty: The chronology is Newton's later account. No endorsement of his broader claim that refracting telescopes could never overcome colour error.
nodes.date_basis: Newton's 1672 paper retrospectively dates the initial prism investigations to the beginning of 1666; not contemporaneous publication.

nodes.title: Carnot’s heat-engine analysis
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: A reversible-cycle argument that, for a given quantity of caloric transferred, the maximum obtainable work depends on the reservoir temperatures rather than the working substance, developed while examining existing heat engines and their improvement.
nodes.uncertainty: Carnot's published argument uses conserved caloric. It is not the modern energy-conservation formulation or a claim that he supplied an already implemented engine design. Inspected passages, not the entire book.
nodes.date_basis: Publication of Réflexions sur la puissance motrice du feu, Paris, Bachelier.

nodes.title: Clapeyron’s analytic heat cycle
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Clapeyron explicitly takes Carnot's reasoning as his starting point and expresses cycle work through pressure–volume geometry and mathematical analysis.
nodes.uncertainty: The early caloric framework is retained; this node is not the complete modern second law. Original French pp. 153–157 read in scan/OCR; p. 155 visually verified. English 1837 translation passages were also consulted.
nodes.date_basis: Original memoir in Journal de l'École polytechnique, tome XIV, cahier XXIII, pp. 153–190; date confirmed by BnF record.

nodes.title: Clausius’s heat-work reconciliation
nodes.anchor_rationale: The February communication is the selected scientific milestone; the separately evidenced publication interval is retained.
nodes.summary: Clausius combined equivalence of heat and work with a modified Carnot argument: part of the heat can be converted to work while another part passes from a warmer body to a colder one.
nodes.uncertainty: Read in the 1867 English collection. Bracketed 1864 additions are excluded. The 1850 node is not the later naming of entropy; other contributors and parallel approaches remain outside this subset.
nodes.date_basis: The First Memoir editorial note distinguishes February communication from March–April publication.

nodes.title: Regnault’s steam measurements
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: Published measurements of saturated-steam pressure and latent heat per unit mass, undertaken for steam-engine calculations; Thomson describes the published range as 0–230 °C and the missing density information needed for his calculations.
nodes.uncertainty: The recipient’s contemporary account and bibliographic record were inspected; Regnault’s underlying experimental volume was not retrieved (Gallica 403). No claim of auditing its apparatus or tables.
nodes.date_basis: First published volume of the government-commissioned Relation des expériences, as identified contemporaneously by Thomson. Individual measurement dates are not assigned.

nodes.title: Thomson’s first absolute scale
nodes.anchor_rationale: Use this specifically evidenced scientific milestone, retaining date-basis and review qualifications; no unique universal discovery date asserted.
nodes.summary: A thermometric scale in which a unit of heat descending through any one degree yields the same mechanical effect, constructed from Carnot-style reasoning and an approximate use of Regnault’s steam data.
nodes.uncertainty: This caloric-based 1848 proposal is not the later linear Kelvin scale. Thomson still expresses doubt about heat/work conversion and lacks reliable saturated-vapour densities across the full range.
nodes.date_basis: October 1848 Philosophical Magazine, vol. 33, pp. 313–317. This dates the published proposal.

nodes.title: Thomson’s Carnot calculations
nodes.anchor_rationale: The original account’s explicit presentation date anchors this scientific episode; the distinct comparison remains a separately dated appendix event.
nodes.summary: On 2 January 1849 Thomson presented an account using Regnault’s steam observations, discussing Joule while provisionally retaining caloric conservation. In an appendix read 30 April 1849, he compared Regnault-derived values with Carnot’s and Clapeyron’s earlier results.
nodes.uncertainty: Later bracketed notes in the collected edition are excluded from the 1849 proposition. Quoting Carnot does not by itself establish physical access to a particular copy.
nodes.date_basis: Explicit read date printed with the original account; distinct from the later appendix.

nodes.title: Ra I experimental papyrus vessel
nodes.anchor_rationale: The documented departure on the experimental voyage is a practical deployment of the single nonmarket research vessel, distinct from its construction and abandonment.
nodes.summary: The specific 1969 Ra papyrus-reed vessel used by Thor Heyerdahl’s expedition, distinct from the later Ra II.
nodes.uncertainty: The expedition tests a particular modern voyage; it cannot establish prehistoric transatlantic contact. Ra II was a new vessel; no abandonment of the reed-boat family is claimed.
nodes.date_basis: The 22 July 1969 participant interview reports departure from Safi on May 25.

bio-human-genome-draft-2000--event-01.date_basis: Anchored to the 7 October 2000 data snapshot analysed in the February 2001 paper.
bio-human-genome-draft-2000--event-01.statement: The public consortium’s assembled draft provided broad human genome sequence coverage while retaining gaps and ambiguities.

bio-human-hierarchical-sequencing-1999--.date_basis: Dates the public consortium’s production phase and procedures used for the October 2000 draft, not invention of shotgun sequencing.
bio-human-hierarchical-sequencing-1999--.statement: The public consortium sequenced mapped BAC/PAC clones with automated fluorescent reads and computational assembly.

bio-humidity-varied-dna-diffraction-1952.date_basis: Archive dates the original B-form image to 1952; the humidity-dependent procedure is documented by the signed 2 April 1953 account.
bio-humidity-varied-dna-diffraction-1952.statement: Franklin and Gosling obtained DNA-fibre X-ray patterns under differing hydration, distinguishing crystalline A and wetter B configurations.

bio-insect-virus-base-ratios-1952--event.date_basis: Measurements were reported in a manuscript received 1 July 1952; bounded as established by that year, without claiming the earliest such measurements.
bio-insect-virus-base-ratios-1952--event.statement: Wyatt’s analyses of DNA from 11 insect viruses found A:T and G:C near unity while aggregate base composition varied.

bio-phix174-sequence-report-1977--event-.date_basis: Node is the public sequence report of 24 February 1977; exact completion of all contributing experiments is not established by the inspected abstract.
bio-phix174-sequence-report-1977--event-.statement: A reported approximately 5,375-nucleotide φX174 sequence, obtained with plus/minus sequencing, revealed overlapping coding regions.

bio-plus-minus-sequencing-1974--event-01.date_basis: Demonstrations appear in a manuscript received 20 December 1974; publication followed in May 1975.
bio-plus-minus-sequencing-1974--event-01.statement: Sanger and Coulson used primed DNA synthesis, limiting nucleotide conditions, E. coli and T4 polymerases, and gel separation to infer sequences.

bio-template-directed-synthesis-1959--ev.date_basis: The 1959 lecture synthesizes the 1958 cited enzyme studies and then-current template evidence; interval marks that evidence/interpretation stage.
bio-template-directed-synthesis-1959--ev.statement: Kornberg’s team interpreted DNA-dependent enzymatic synthesis as copying through complementary base pairing and presented several experimental lines of support.

elec-ampere-parallel-currents-1820--even.date_basis: Composite memoir read 2 October includes communications of 18 and 25 September; exact experimental day not recovered.
elec-ampere-parallel-currents-1820--even.statement: Two parallel straight conductor sections, one counterweighted and movable, carry currents from two voltaic piles; same-direction currents attract and opposite-direction currents repel.

elec-atalla-kahng-mos-1959--event-01.date_basis: Museum narrative dates successful fabrication to 1959; the 1960 meeting report is corroborated by Moore’s account.
elec-atalla-kahng-mos-1959--event-01.statement: Atalla and Kahng demonstrated a silicon field-effect transistor with an oxide-insulated gate controlling conduction between source and drain.

elec-bardeen-surface-states-1946--event-.date_basis: Museum dates the proposal one year after the April 1945 experiment; the contemporary paper appeared in May 1947.
elec-bardeen-surface-states-1946--event-.statement: Bardeen proposed that electronic states at a semiconductor surface could screen an applied field; his published contact model included surface charge and space charge.

elec-branly-filings-detector-c1890--even.date_basis: Museum dates the filings device to about 1890; interval encodes that approximate attribution, not measured calendar bounds.
elec-branly-filings-detector-c1890--even.statement: A granular metallic-contact device whose conductivity changes under electrical disturbance; this filings device is the predecessor Marconi calls a Branly coherer.

elec-fairchild-junction-isolation-1960--.date_basis: Working boron-diffused isolation circuits dated 27 September; public Micrologic announcement followed March 1961.
elec-fairchild-junction-isolation-1960--.statement: Haas and Kattner’s boron-diffusion isolation process produced working flip-flop circuits using p–n junction separation.

elec-fairchild-physical-isolation-1960--.date_basis: Working monolithic devices dated 26 May by the museum; not the 1961 public announcement.
elec-fairchild-physical-isolation-1960--.statement: Jay Last’s team made the Norman flip-flop using rear-etched channels filled with insulating epoxy to separate circuit components.

elec-fairchild-silicon-gate-3708-1968--e.date_basis: Commercial 3708 introduction in 1968; abbreviated technical presentation in October 1968, full paper in 1970.
elec-fairchild-silicon-gate-3708-1968--e.statement: Faggin and Klein brought polysilicon-gate processing to ICs; Faggin redesigned an eight-channel analog multiplexer as the Fairchild 3708.

elec-faraday-disc-generator-1831--event-.date_basis: Working generator described in First Series read 24 November 1831; specific October dates are not asserted.
elec-faraday-disc-generator-1831--event-.statement: A rotating copper disc passes between concentrated magnetic poles; sliding collectors at rim and axle feed a galvanometer, sustaining a deflection while rotation continues.

elec-faraday-moving-magnet-1831--event-0.date_basis: First Series read 24 November 1831 reports the performed test; no exact day inferred from paragraph order.
elec-faraday-moving-magnet-1831--event-0.statement: A cylindrical permanent magnet is inserted into and withdrawn from a hollow coil connected to a galvanometer; motion gives opposite current impulses, and a stationary magnet gives none.

elec-faraday-ring-induction-1831--event-.date_basis: Museum dates successful ring experiment to 29 August 1831; First Series gives the experimental configuration.
elec-faraday-ring-induction-1831--event-.statement: Separately insulated windings around an iron ring connect to a battery and a remote galvanometer. Making or breaking the battery circuit gives opposite transient responses; steady current gives no sustained deflection.

elec-faraday-rotation-1821--event-01.date_basis: Diary entries for 3 and 4 September 1821 quoted by the Royal Institution.
elec-faraday-rotation-1821--event-01.statement: A battery-fed wire maintains contact through mercury while moving continuously around a magnetic pole; the following day’s arrangement improves wire and magnet support.

elec-helmholtz-dielectric-test-1879--eve.date_basis: Hertz’s retrospective introduction dates the Berlin Academy prize problem to 1879.
elec-helmholtz-dielectric-test-1879--eve.statement: A proposed experiment seeks a relation between dielectric polarization and electromagnetic force, testing assumptions that connect Helmholtz’s electrodynamics to Maxwell’s equations.

elec-hertz-air-wave-reflection-1888--eve.date_basis: Follows the November 1887 dielectric work and is reported in the 1888 air-wave paper; this interval avoids equating publication year with an unverified exact performance date.
elec-hertz-air-wave-reflection-1888--eve.statement: A spark oscillator illuminates a metal reflecting wall; moving and turning a spark-gap loop detects spatial strengthening and weakening consistent with incident/reflected waves.

elec-hertz-spark-apparatus-1886-1887--ev.date_basis: Hertz dates the triggering observation to spring 1886 and the dielectric-test result to 10 November 1887.
elec-hertz-spark-apparatus-1886-1887--ev.statement: Induction-coil-driven spark oscillators and nearly closed secondary conductors with small adjustable gaps reveal rapid electrical oscillations; conductor placement is revised for dielectric tests.

elec-hoerni-planar-conception-1957--even.date_basis: Notebook conception dated December 1957 by the museum; not yet a working transistor.
elec-hoerni-planar-conception-1957--even.statement: Hoerni proposed leaving oxide over the junction edges while opening contact areas, instead of stripping the oxide after diffusion.

elec-hoerni-planar-transistor-1959--even.date_basis: Working device dated March 1959; patent filed May 1959; commercial 2N1613 came in 1960.
elec-hoerni-planar-transistor-1959--even.statement: Hoerni implemented a silicon transistor whose diffused junction edges remained protected by oxide, with patterned contact openings.

elec-intel-4004-cpu-1971--event-01.date_basis: Working/commercial CPU implementation dated 1971 in the museum history.
elec-intel-4004-cpu-1971--event-01.statement: The MCS-4 family’s CPU function was implemented on the 4004 silicon-gate chip; Hoff and Mazor developed the architecture and Faggin with Shima implemented the design.

elec-kilby-germanium-oscillator-1958--ev.date_basis: Museum dates the working oscillator to 12 September 1958.
elec-kilby-germanium-oscillator-1958--ev.statement: Kilby connected germanium transistor, capacitor and resistor elements with fine gold wires to make an oscillator.

elec-marconi-aerial-earth-1895--event-01.date_basis: Marconi retrospectively dates the new arrangement to August 1895.
elec-marconi-aerial-earth-1895--event-01.statement: One oscillator terminal connects to earth and the other to an elevated conductor; the receiver similarly connects its coherer between earth and an elevated conductor. Telegraph key, relay and tapping receiver apparatus support signs.

elec-marconi-initial-tests-1895--event-0.date_basis: Marconi’s 1909 lecture dates the initial home experiments to early 1895.
elec-marconi-initial-tests-1895--event-0.statement: An ordinary Hertz oscillator and Branly coherer are combined in preliminary tests aimed at transmitting telegraphic signs without connecting wires.

elec-maxwell-field-theory-1864--event-01.date_basis: Received 27 October and read 8 December 1864; expanded paper published 1865.
elec-maxwell-field-theory-1864--event-01.statement: A dynamical field formulation incorporates induction and electric displacement, yielding transverse disturbances with a calculated speed compared with optical measurements.

elec-noyce-planar-interconnection-1959--.date_basis: Concept developed in 1959 and disclosed in the application filed 30 July; not a working chip at filing.
elec-noyce-planar-interconnection-1959--.statement: Noyce proposed deposited metal conductors crossing retained oxide to connect semiconductor regions without shorting junctions, including multi-device circuits.

elec-oersted-current-magnetism-1820--eve.date_basis: Repeated observations reported by 21 July 1820; day of initial discovery is not assigned.
elec-oersted-current-magnetism-1820--eve.statement: A wire closing a galvanic circuit deflects a nearby suspended magnetic needle; moving the wire above/below reverses deflection; nonmagnetic needles provide controls.

elec-oersted-trough-battery-1820--event-.date_basis: Working apparatus specified in the report signed 21 July 1820.
elec-oersted-trough-battery-1820--event-.statement: Twenty copper troughs with copper connections supporting zinc plates in the next trough; water with sulfuric and nitric acids; sufficient current for the closed-wire needle experiment.

elec-oxide-diffusion-mask-1955--event-01.date_basis: Experimental development in 1955; patent/publication followed in 1957.
elec-oxide-diffusion-mask-1955--event-01.statement: Frosch and Derick used silicon dioxide to protect wafers and delimit dopant diffusion through etched openings.

elec-oxide-surface-stabilization-1958--e.date_basis: A 1958 ECS report is discussed in the Moore/Last oral history; the full experimental paper was received January 1959 and published May 1959.
elec-oxide-surface-stabilization-1958--e.statement: Atalla, Tannenbaum and Scheibner measured thermally oxidized silicon interfaces and device behavior, finding stable surface potentials with characteristic interface states.

elec-photolithographic-windows-1955--eve.date_basis: Museum dates Andrus and Bond’s adaptation to 1955; patent filing and later refinements are separate.
elec-photolithographic-windows-1955--eve.statement: Jules Andrus and Walter Bond adapted photoresist patterning to etch windows in silicon oxide before localized diffusion.

elec-point-contact-amplifier-1947--event.date_basis: Successful amplification on 16 December; demonstration to laboratory officials on 23 December, as dated by the museum.
elec-point-contact-amplifier-1947--event.statement: Bardeen and Brattain placed two closely spaced gold contacts against germanium to obtain amplification.

elec-volta-batteries-1800--event-01.date_basis: Dated description of working configurations in the report read 26 June 1800; not a claim that construction began that day.
elec-volta-batteries-1800--event-01.statement: Repeated silver–zinc pairs with saline-wetted separators in a column; an explicitly described alternative connected dissimilar-metal bows through a chain of liquid-filled cups.

glass-ee2-commercial-2019.date_basis: Google dates launch to May; 20 May begins contact with sales/partners and a 21 May trade report says partner availability.
glass-ee2-commercial-2019.statement: Google announced Glass Enterprise Edition 2 on 20 May 2019 and invited enterprise customers to contact its sales team or partners; a 21 May report described partner availability.

glass-ee2-developer-channel-2020.date_basis: Google announced direct reseller purchasing for developers on this day.
glass-ee2-developer-channel-2020.statement: On 4 February 2020 Google said developers and businesses could purchase Glass Enterprise Edition 2 devices directly from named hardware resellers.

glass-ee2-google-withdrawal-2023.date_basis: Google says that as of 15 March it would no longer sell the family. This establishes a latest cessation date, not the exact first day without sales.
glass-ee2-google-withdrawal-2023.statement: By 15 March 2023 Google was no longer selling Glass Enterprise Edition, including Edition 2; reseller withdrawal and last actual device use are not established.

glass-ee2-support-cutoff-2023.date_basis: Google states support/replacement under the described process continues until this date.
glass-ee2-support-cutoff-2023.statement: Google identified a support and replacement cutoff for Glass Enterprise Edition.

glass-ee2-test-2018.date_basis: SGS report records the sample received on this date.
glass-ee2-test-2018.statement: The test laboratory received a Glass Enterprise Edition 2 GG2 sample.

global-arelate-southern-aqueduct--event-.date_basis: The 2018 site account states this interval of city-supply use; original construction is not independently dated.
global-arelate-southern-aqueduct--event-.statement: Southern spring-fed aqueduct branch supplying Arelate before diversion to Barbegal.

global-barbegal-aqueduct-mills--event-01.date_basis: The 2018 site account dates diversion to the new mills around 120–130; the 2024 account retains a second-century placement.
global-barbegal-aqueduct-mills--event-01.statement: Two rows of eight watermills supplied by the redirected southern aqueduct branch.

global-bi-sheng-alternating-reuse--event.date_basis: Shen Gua retrospectively attributes the reported workflow to the Qingli reign; anchor is only a display midpoint.
global-bi-sheng-alternating-reuse--event.statement: Two forms alternate composition and printing; reheating releases characters for storage and reuse.

global-bi-sheng-assembled-form--event-01.date_basis: Shen Gua retrospectively attributes the reported workflow to the Qingli reign; anchor is only a display midpoint.
global-bi-sheng-assembled-form--event-01.statement: Fired types composed within a frame on a coated iron plate, warmed and leveled.

global-bi-sheng-fired-types--event-01.date_basis: Shen Gua retrospectively attributes the reported workflow to the Qingli reign; anchor is only a display midpoint.
global-bi-sheng-fired-types--event-01.statement: Bi Sheng’s separately carved clay characters, hardened by firing, as reported by Shen Gua.

global-dholavira-reservoirs-stage3--even.date_basis: ICOMOS assigns the reservoir expansion to archaeological Stage III; midpoint is display placement, not a dated year.
global-dholavira-reservoirs-stage3--even.statement: Reservoirs east, south and west of the Castle, constructed during the Stage III urban expansion.

global-diamond-sutra-paper-print-868--ev.date_basis: The artifact’s colophon is converted by its custodian to 11 May 868.
global-diamond-sutra-paper-print-868--ev.statement: Seven woodblock-printed paper sheets joined into a scroll; the custodian identifies hemp and mulberry paper.

global-hokulea-built-1975--launch-1975.date_basis: The operating institution gives the launch date and place.
global-hokulea-built-1975--launch-1975.statement: Hōkūleʻa was launched on 8 March 1975 at Hakipuʻu-Kualoa, Kāneʻohe Bay, Oʻahu.

global-hokulea-built-1975--practical-197.date_basis: PVS voyage timeline gives the outbound departure from Honolua Bay.
global-hokulea-built-1975--practical-197.statement: The PVS canoe departed on its Hawaiʻi–Tahiti research voyage, guided by Mau Piailug using non-instrument wayfinding.

global-hokulea-built-1975--production-by.date_basis: The documented 8 March launch establishes that the vessel had been built by then; the inspected sources do not establish a specific construction-completion date.
global-hokulea-built-1975--production-by.statement: Hōkūleʻa had been built by its launch on 8 March 1975.

global-hokulea-design-study-1973--event-.date_basis: Low’s participant interview account dates the design project’s start to early 1973; Kāne describes the reasoning retrospectively.
global-hokulea-design-study-1973--event-.statement: Kāne and Emory selected widely recorded canoe features as a hypothesis about earlier forms for an experimental vessel.

global-hokulea-wayfinding-trial-1980--ev.date_basis: Contemporaneous Kyselka report dates the outward-and-return voyage to March–June 1980.
global-hokulea-wayfinding-trial-1980--ev.statement: Voyage tested learned wayfinding and planetarium-derived cues; estimates were recorded and radioed to an escort for plotting and comparison.

global-jikji-metal-type-1377--event-01.date_basis: Custodian attributes this surviving volume to Heungdeok-sa printing in 1377.
global-jikji-metal-type-1377--event-01.statement: Surviving second volume of Jikji, printed using movable cast-metal characters.

global-jikji-woodblock-1378--event-01.date_basis: Custodian identifies the preserved Ch’wi’am xylograph edition as dated 1378.
global-jikji-woodblock-1378--event-01.statement: Complete text of Jikji in a preserved woodblock edition.

global-korent-wavefinding-2005--event-01.date_basis: Original article dates ethnographic fieldwork and observed practice to June 2005–September 2006.
global-korent-wavefinding-2005--event-01.statement: Korent Joel demonstrated wave-based landfinding during field collaboration, including navigation of a yacht between atolls.

global-malindi-assisted-passage-1498--ev.date_basis: Voyage narrative places departure on 24 April, land sighting on 18 May and identification/arrival on 20 May.
global-malindi-assisted-passage-1498--ev.statement: A pilot supplied at Malindi guided Vasco da Gama’s fleet across the Arabian Sea and interpreted coastal landmarks.

global-marshall-cross-swell-observation-.date_basis: WAM’s participant interview places buoy deployments during the field year beginning in 2005 and culminating in the 2006 voyage; the research paper also states a June 2005–September 2006 fieldwork interval. Exact deployment days are not given.
global-marshall-cross-swell-observation-.statement: Navigator-identified vessel rocking and directional wave measurements were consistent with bent incident swells; multiple wave trains limited field validation.

global-marshall-waverider-survey--event-.date_basis: WAM’s participant interview places buoy deployments during the field year beginning in 2005 and culminating in the 2006 voyage; the research paper also states a June 2005–September 2006 fieldwork interval. Exact deployment days are not given.
global-marshall-waverider-survey--event-.statement: Datawell Directional Waverider G-4 deployments at navigator-selected wave patterns; GPS motion sensing produced directional spectra.

global-mau-hokulea-passage-1976--event-0.date_basis: Kyselka’s 1980 account and PVS history date Mau’s guiding voyage to 1976.
global-mau-hokulea-passage-1976--event-0.statement: Mau Piailug guided Hōkūleʻa to Tahiti using noninstrument wayfinding.

global-mau-thompson-teaching-1979--event.date_basis: Kyselka dates Thompson’s Micronesia visit to March 1979; PVS dates Mau’s return to Hawaiʻi to teach in that year.
global-mau-thompson-teaching-1979--event.statement: Mau taught Nainoa Thompson and collaborators to integrate wind, waves, swells, birds and stars in wayfinding.

global-muldoons-channel-infill--event-01.date_basis: Rounded combined calibrated ranges of basal infill samples OZL608/OZL760, c. 6450–6740 cal BP (BP=1950), constrain prior excavation. This dates evidence of an existing channel, not its invention.
global-muldoons-channel-infill--event-01.statement: Bifurcated channel F10 created by removal of basalt blocks; dated basal infill establishes an earlier excavated form.

global-muldoons-walled-channel--event-01.date_basis: Article assigns walls to c. 600–800 cal BP; conversion uses BP=1950.
global-muldoons-walled-channel--event-01.statement: Multi-tiered basalt walls added along the pre-existing F10 channel.

global-planetarium-latitude-method-1980-.date_basis: The participant account identifies this as preparation already used on the voyage that left on 15 March 1980; the study’s starting date is not established.
global-planetarium-latitude-method-1980-.statement: Thompson and Kyselka varied simulated latitude to study star rise/set positions and candidate latitude cues.

global-rome-aqueduct-mills-537--event-01.date_basis: Operational stage at the opening of the 537–538 siege; Procopius’s narrative sequence, with calendar placement checked in Bury.
global-rome-aqueduct-mills-537--event-01.statement: Hill mills powered by descending aqueduct water, operating before the siege’s supply cut.

global-rome-boat-mills-537--practical-53.date_basis: Procopius narrates the response at the beginning of the siege; Bury places this episode in 537.
global-rome-boat-mills-537--practical-53.statement: Procopius reports that mill machinery on moored boats operated in the Tiber to grind flour during the siege.

global-rome-protected-boat-mills-537--ev.date_basis: Operational stage at the opening of the 537–538 siege; Procopius’s narrative sequence, with calendar placement checked in Bury.
global-rome-protected-boat-mills-537--ev.statement: Operating boat mills accompanied by an upstream iron-chain debris barrier and removal crew.

hoerni-conception-1957.statement: Hoerni recorded a method to protect exposed silicon transistor junctions with retained oxide.

hoerni-prototype-1959.date_basis: IEEE places the demonstration the week after a 2 March notebook entry; Chip History gives 12 March.
hoerni-prototype-1959.statement: Hoerni demonstrated an early planar transistor prototype.

intel-4004-merchant-1971.date_basis: Intel advertisement reports the MCS-4 family in stock on this day.
intel-4004-merchant-1971.statement: On 15 November 1971 Intel advertised the MCS-4 family, including the 4004, as in stock for its merchant market.

intel-4004-prototype-1971.date_basis: Participant account describes working wafer run in January and subsequent correction of minor bugs.
intel-4004-prototype-1971.statement: A 4004 silicon run worked in January 1971; subsequent tests found and corrected minor errors.

mat-abbe-compensating-eyepieces-1886--ev.date_basis: Abbe explains the construction in his 1886 paper; Zeiss retrospectively dates the named eyepiece introduction with the objectives to August 1886.
mat-abbe-compensating-eyepieces-1886--ev.statement: Eyepieces deliberately given a color-dependent magnification opposite to the remaining lateral color difference of the objective, so the combined microscope image has less color error away from the axis.

mat-basic-bessemer-lining--event-01.date_basis: Blaenavon experiments from 1877, reported success in March 1878, subsequent Middlesbrough refinement in 1879.
mat-basic-bessemer-lining--event-01.statement: Thomas and Gilchrist modified the converter lining to remove phosphorus during Bessemer steelmaking.

mat-belovode-copper-smelting--event-01.date_basis: Trench 3, occupation horizon D / Gradac phase; archaeological phase range reported by excavators.
mat-belovode-copper-smelting--event-01.statement: Copper-bearing slag and slagged ceramic sherds document extraction of copper from ore at a Vinča settlement.

mat-bessemer-air-conversion--event-01.date_basis: Patent year specified in the Science Museum collection record; not the date of universal commercial reliability.
mat-bessemer-air-conversion--event-01.statement: Air blown through molten pig iron in a converter; oxidation supplies heat during conversion to steel.

mat-dallinger-optical-comparisons-1887--.date_basis: The tests followed the 1886 instrument introductions and preceded Dallinger’s address on 9 February 1887; exact individual test dates are not supplied.
mat-dallinger-optical-comparisons-1887--.statement: Dallinger compared Zeiss objectives and compensating eyepieces with his existing high-power lenses, including trials swapping in the new eyepieces; he and Mayall also recorded independent judgments on a supplied series.

mat-edsken-bessemer-implementation--even.date_basis: Practical-scale implementation at Edsken dated by the Swedish steel industry historical account.
mat-edsken-bessemer-implementation--even.statement: Göran Fredrik Göransson applied the Bessemer method on a practical scale and obtained satisfactory steel ingots.

mat-faraday-heavy-optical-glass-1829--ev.date_basis: Faraday dates the dedicated heavy-glass work from September 1828 and describes the established preparation in his lecture read in late 1829.
mat-faraday-heavy-optical-glass-1829--ev.statement: Faraday’s silicated borate of lead: a heavy optical glass finished and annealed in platinum trays after purification, mixing and fusion of the constituents.

mat-faraday-magneto-optic-rotation-1845-.date_basis: The paper was received on 6 November 1845 and describes the inquiry as recently resumed; the inspected passage establishes an observation by 1845, not its precise experimental date.
mat-faraday-magneto-optic-rotation-1845-.statement: Polarized light traversing Faraday’s heavy glass along a magnetic field changed its plane of polarization; reversing the magnetic poles reversed the rotation.

mat-gerlafingen-oxygen-trials--event-01.date_basis: ASME history caption dates the experimental top-blown converter to 1948.
mat-gerlafingen-oxygen-trials--event-01.statement: Robert Durrer’s experimental converter applied oxygen from above the iron bath.

mat-gerzeh-meteoritic-iron--event-01.date_basis: Closed burials assigned to Naqada IIC–IIIA, approximately 3400–3100 BCE; abstract rounds to 3200 BCE.
mat-gerzeh-meteoritic-iron--event-01.statement: Meteoritic iron hammered into sheet and rolled into tubular beads; a metalworking route requiring no extraction of iron from ore.

mat-great-lakes-native-copper-tools--eve.date_basis: Rounded conversion of the reported 8500–3580 cal BP range for embedded organics, using the 1950 BP epoch; an evidence span, not the lifetime of one culture.
mat-great-lakes-native-copper-tools--eve.statement: Large utilitarian tools forged from native copper; dated organic material remains embedded in some copper artifacts.

mat-jena-new-optical-glasses-1886--event.date_basis: Abbe’s 1886 report states that the Jena factory had already commenced manufacture for general optical use; this is an attested availability date, not a claim that production began in 1886.
mat-jena-new-optical-glasses-1886--event.statement: The Jena Glastechnisches Laboratorium supplied a wider selection of optical glasses, including borate and phosphate compositions with varied refractive-index and dispersion combinations.

mat-jena-spectrometric-glass-research-18.date_basis: Abbe’s account presented in 1886 explicitly says the Schott–Abbe investigation began in 1881; the interval covers the program reported there.
mat-jena-spectrometric-glass-research-18.statement: Schott and Abbe, with Zeiss workshop cooperation, measured experimental glass melts spectrometrically to relate composition to refractive and dispersive properties and select further compositions.

mat-linz-ld-production--event-01.statement: An operating LD plant converted carbon-rich hot metal into lower-carbon steel by oxygen blowing.

mat-linz-soft-blowing-trials--event-01.date_basis: VÖEST chronology: trials began 3 June; changed lance position and pressure on 25 June; larger experimental vessel in October.
mat-linz-soft-blowing-trials--event-01.statement: Lower oxygen pressure and a more distant lance yielded steel suitable for rolling into sheet in converter trials.

mat-merv-crucible-cofusion--event-01.date_basis: Workshop assigned by the excavators to the ninth–early tenth century; 930 is a display bound for early tenth, not a measured endpoint.
mat-merv-crucible-cofusion--event-01.statement: Workshop crucibles interpreted as evidence for combining cast iron and wrought iron to produce steel.

mat-plocnik-tainted-ore-bronze--event-01.date_basis: Occupation-horizon date is a terminus ante quem for the foil, not a direct measurement of its manufacture.
mat-plocnik-tainted-ore-bronze--event-01.statement: Tin-bronze foil interpreted as metal smelted from complex copper–tin ores, subsequently worked and annealed.

mat-powell-lealand-apochromat-1886--even.date_basis: In his address of 9 February 1887 Dallinger recalls the objective and eyepieces displayed at the Society’s November meeting, hence November 1886.
mat-powell-lealand-apochromat-1886--even.statement: Powell and Lealand made a 1/12-inch apochromatic objective to their own formula, with compensating eyepieces constructed on Abbe's plan; the combination was exhibited at the Society's November 1886 meeting.

mat-qiwu-reported-cofusion--event-01.date_basis: Practice assigned retrospectively to Qiwu Huaiwen in Beishi, chapter 89; this is the reported sixth-century activity, not the later compilation date.
mat-qiwu-reported-cofusion--event-01.statement: A biography describes heating powdered cast iron with soft-iron blanks for several days to make steel for sabres.

mat-ri-glass-furnace-1827--event-01.date_basis: Faraday reports the room and furnaces built in September 1827; the surviving notebook is headed October 1827.
mat-ri-glass-furnace-1827--event-01.statement: A dedicated experimental room and furnaces brought Faraday’s optical-glass experiments onto the Royal Institution premises, with Sergeant Anderson assisting.

mat-zeiss-apochromatic-objectives-1886--.date_basis: The 1889 manufacturer catalogue dates introduction to August 1886; Abbe’s 1886 report describes their construction and performance aims.
mat-zeiss-apochromatic-objectives-1886--.statement: A manufactured series of microscope objectives using new glass materials and optical formulae, designed to improve chromatic and spherical correction and paired with compensating eyepieces.

mat-zhou-bronze-iron-bolt--event-01.date_basis: Same CB3 attribution as its shaft; these are two production stages evidenced by one object.
mat-zhou-bronze-iron-bolt--event-01.statement: CB3 combines a leaded-bronze head with the treated iron shaft.

mat-zhou-cast-decarburized-shaft--event-.date_basis: CB3 museum attribution: fifth–fourth centuries BCE, Eastern Zhou; manufacture dated by the artifact attribution.
mat-zhou-cast-decarburized-shaft--event-.statement: CB3 shaft: cast to rod shape, then decarburized to low-carbon iron.

math-allen-circles-proportion-1635--even.date_basis: Whipple catalogue accession 0833 dates the surviving instrument c.1635; decade bounds encode approximate dating, not a measured manufacturing interval.
math-allen-circles-proportion-1635--even.statement: Surviving brass circular logarithmic instrument made by Elias Allen to Oughtred's design, using fixed concentric scales and paired radial index arms.

math-brahmagupta-zero-rules-628--event-0.date_basis: Composition date supplied by the edited-text header; the surviving editions and translation are much later.
math-brahmagupta-zero-rules-628--event-0.statement: Brāhmasphuṭasiddhānta chapter 18 treats positive, negative and zero quantities in addition, subtraction and multiplication; a multiplied quantity times zero gives zero.

math-briggs-common-logarithms-1617--even.date_basis: Publication of Logarithmorum Chilias Prima in London after the 1615–1616 discussions with Napier.
math-briggs-common-logarithms-1617--even.statement: Published common-logarithm tables following discussion and revision of Napier's scheme; the node is the 1617 publication, not sole attribution of the idea.

math-bugia-numeral-instruction-before120.date_basis: Leonardo retrospectively places this instruction in his childhood before composing Liber abaci in 1202. The biographical birth estimate of about 1170 does not establish a hard lower bound for the lesson; no exact lesson year is attested.
math-bugia-numeral-instruction-before120.statement: Leonardo Pisano reports receiving instruction in calculation with the nine Indian figures while his father served the Pisan merchant community at Bugia.

math-dutch-spyglass-1608--event-01.date_basis: Lipperhey's demonstration and the States General record of 2 October 1608; does not date a unique invention event.
math-dutch-spyglass-1608--event-01.statement: A working distance-magnifying spyglass presented by Hans Lipperhey and recorded in a patent request; other maker claims remain distinct.

math-galileo-improved-telescope-1609--ev.date_basis: Construction and improvement ran from 1609 into early 1610; lunar and planetary observing configurations were attained at different points.
math-galileo-improved-telescope-1609--ev.statement: Galileo's progressively improved convex-objective/concave-eyepiece telescopes, with selected or manufactured lenses adequate for his lunar and later planetary observations.

math-galileo-jupiter-satellites-1610--ev.date_basis: Dated observations begin 7 January; four objects are recorded on 13 January; interpretation follows the changing positions.
math-galileo-jupiter-satellites-1610--ev.statement: Repeated telescopic positions of objects near Jupiter, interpreted as four bodies revolving around it rather than fixed stars.

math-galileo-lunar-relief-1609--event-01.date_basis: Museo Galileo dates the surviving Moon drawings to November–December 1609; the interpretation was published in 1610.
math-galileo-lunar-relief-1609--event-01.statement: Repeated telescopic views of the lunar light-shadow boundary and isolated illuminated features interpreted as an uneven surface with elevations and depressions.

math-gunter-logarithmic-scale-1620--even.date_basis: Retrospective museum date for introduction of logarithmic rules used with dividers, not a dated surviving specimen.
math-gunter-logarithmic-scale-1620--even.statement: A physical logarithmically divided rule on which a pair of dividers transfers distances to calculate.

math-hawari-worked-arithmetic-1305--even.date_basis: The work states completion on 18 Dhu al-Qaʿda 704 AH, interpreted by the editors as 12 June 1305 Julian; surviving copies are later.
math-hawari-worked-arithmetic-1305--even.statement: Worked computational illustrations of Ibn al-Banna's rules, including 4043 + 2685 = 6728 with a zero place and explicit carrying between ranks.

math-ibn-banna-condensed-arithmetic-befo.date_basis: The critical edition says shortly before 1301; 1256 is the author's birth and only a conservative lower bound. The anchor near 1300 is approximate, not an attested composition year.
math-ibn-banna-condensed-arithmetic-befo.statement: Condensed Book on the Operations of Arithmetic gives rules for known and unknown quantities, including place-aligned addition, without worked numerical examples.

math-khwarizmi-indian-arithmetic-825--ev.date_basis: Folkerts places composition in the first half of the ninth century in Baghdad; 825 is a conventional midpoint, not an exact dated manuscript.
math-khwarizmi-indian-arithmetic-825--ev.statement: Arithmetic procedures using nine numeral signs and decimal places, with a small circle for an empty place, attributed to Indian reckoning in the later Latin textual tradition.

math-latin-dixit-algorizmi-1100s--event-.date_basis: Folkerts dates the Latin translation and redaction to the twelfth century; the anchor is a display midpoint. Surviving manuscript copies are later.
math-latin-dixit-algorizmi-1100s--event-.statement: Latin reworking of al-Khwarizmi-derived arithmetic, preserving decimal positions, nine numeral signs and a small-circle placeholder; includes operational arithmetic rules.

math-latin-liber-alchorismi-1100s--event.date_basis: Folkerts groups the work among twelfth-century Latin adaptations; no exact composition year is established.
math-latin-liber-alchorismi-1100s--event.statement: A separate Latin arithmetic exposition expanding and arranging al-Khwarizmi-derived calculation methods, including operations on integers and fractions and square-root extraction.

math-liber-abaci-revision-1228--event-01.date_basis: Dates the surviving revised work, not the lost first redaction of 1202 or the date of its later manuscript copies.
math-liber-abaci-revision-1228--event-01.statement: The revised Liber abaci teaches writing numbers with nine figures plus 0, decimal place values and explicit empty-place examples such as 209, alongside arithmetic procedures.

math-napier-logarithms-1614--event-01.date_basis: Publication of Mirifici logarithmorum canonis descriptio; not the beginning of Napier's decades of work.
math-napier-logarithms-1614--event-01.statement: Published logarithmic calculation and tables, in Napier's original normalization rather than modern base-10 form.

math-newton-differential-refraction-1666.date_basis: Newton's 1672 paper retrospectively dates the initial prism investigations to the beginning of 1666; not contemporaneous publication.
math-newton-differential-refraction-1666.statement: Prism investigations leading Newton to identify differing refrangibility among components of sunlight and to diagnose a limitation of simple refracting objectives.

math-newton-reflector-1668--event-01.date_basis: Museo Galileo dates the first construction to 1668; Newton's 1672 account distinguishes it from the later instrument sent to London.
math-newton-reflector-1668--event-01.statement: A telescope Newton built with a polished metal reflecting objective, avoiding refraction at the objective; distinct from the later Royal Society instrument.

math-oughtred-sliding-scales-1620s--even.date_basis: Whipple dates the attributed sliding-scale invention only to the 1620s; the anchor is a display midpoint, not a documented year.
math-oughtred-sliding-scales-1620s--even.statement: Two Gunter-type logarithmic scales moved alongside one another so their relative displacement replaces transfer with dividers.

math-uqlidisi-board-reckoning-952--event.date_basis: Composition of Chapters on Indian Arithmetic in Damascus, dated 341 AH; this is a textual attestation, not the invention of board calculation.
math-uqlidisi-board-reckoning-952--event.statement: The erasable-board arithmetic taken as the starting configuration in al-Uqlidisi's treatment: digits and intermediate results can be erased or shifted during calculation.

math-uqlidisi-paper-reckoning-952--event.date_basis: Book IV of the work composed in 341 AH; the date belongs to the description rather than demonstrated widespread adoption.
math-uqlidisi-paper-reckoning-952--event.statement: Pen-and-paper calculation procedures avoiding the earlier erasure operation; one described multiplication combines Indian operand digits with abjad-written intermediate products.

mech-bersham-through-bar-1775--event-01.date_basis: Bounded by large-cylinder supply ordered in June 1775 for the engine operating in March 1776; the exact commissioning date of the illustrated machine is not established.
mech-bersham-through-bar-1775--event-01.statement: Wilkinson's large-cylinder machining: a stationary cylinder secured on its bed and a rotating boring bar supported beyond both ends, with the cutter fed along the bar.

mech-bloomfield-pump-1776--event-01.date_basis: Engine start reported in Aris's Birmingham Gazette, 11 March 1776, as identified by the archive and technical history.
mech-bloomfield-pump-1776--event-01.statement: Boulton & Watt's single-acting mine-pumping engine at Bloomfield, with a 50-inch cylinder ordered from Wilkinson in June 1775.

mech-carnot-heat-engine-analysis-1824--e.date_basis: Publication of Réflexions sur la puissance motrice du feu, Paris, Bachelier.
mech-carnot-heat-engine-analysis-1824--e.statement: A reversible-cycle argument that, for a given quantity of caloric transferred, the maximum obtainable work depends on the reservoir temperatures rather than the working substance, developed while examining existing heat engines and their improvement.

mech-clapeyron-analytic-cycle-1834--even.date_basis: Original memoir in Journal de l'École polytechnique, tome XIV, cahier XXIII, pp. 153–190; date confirmed by BnF record.
mech-clapeyron-analytic-cycle-1834--even.statement: Clapeyron explicitly takes Carnot's reasoning as his starting point and expresses cycle work through pressure–volume geometry and mathematical analysis.

mech-clausius-heat-work-1850--event-01.date_basis: The First Memoir editorial note distinguishes February communication from March–April publication.
mech-clausius-heat-work-1850--event-01.statement: Clausius communicated the heat-and-work argument in February 1850; publication followed separately.

mech-clausius-heat-work-1850--publicatio.date_basis: The 1867 editorial note reports March–April 1850, while Thomson in 1851 dates the second-part proof to May 1850. The year is supported; the conflicting month reports are preserved.
mech-clausius-heat-work-1850--publicatio.statement: Clausius’s memoir was published in 1850; inspected sources disagree on the publication month of its second part.

mech-condenser-model-1765--event-01.date_basis: Museum attribution of surviving object 1876-1267; this is a model date, not industrial operation.
mech-condenser-model-1765--event-01.statement: Watt's surviving second cylinder-and-separate-condenser model; condensation occurs outside the working cylinder.

mech-condenser-specification-1769--event.date_basis: Patent dated 5 January; specification enrolled 29 April 1769.
mech-condenser-specification-1769--event.statement: Watt's specification couples a hot, insulated steam vessel to a separately cooled condenser and provides for pumps to remove air or other uncondensed elastic vapour.

mech-double-acting-specification-1782--e.date_basis: Patent granted 12 March; specification enrolled 4 July 1782.
mech-double-acting-specification-1782--e.statement: Watt describes alternating steam admission and condensation above and below the piston, transmitting both push and pull through rack-and-sector or other connections.

mech-expansion-specification-1782--event.date_basis: Patent granted 12 March; specification enrolled 4 July 1782.
mech-expansion-specification-1782--event.statement: Watt specifies cutting off admission during the stroke and using steam expansion for the remainder, with a quarter-stroke example and an approximate pressure/work calculation.

mech-joule-equivalent-report-1843--event.date_basis: July 1843 dated paper; August presentation and later 1843 serial publication, distinguished from the 1884 collected edition.
mech-joule-equivalent-report-1843--event.statement: Joule compared mechanical expenditure with heating in magneto-electric experiments, reporting an initial mean equivalent of 838 foot-pounds per pound of water warmed by one Fahrenheit degree, while acknowledging substantial scatter.

mech-joule-friction-calorimeter-1849--ev.date_basis: Apparatus documented in the paper dated 4 June, received 6 June and read 21 June 1849; printed in 1850. Manufacture and individual trial dates are not supplied.
mech-joule-friction-calorimeter-1849--ev.statement: Falling weights drove paddle wheels in calorimetric vessels. Dancer and Fastré thermometers, calibrated using Regnault’s method, measured small rises; separate trials estimated heat leakage, apparatus heat capacity, pulley friction and residual motion.

mech-joule-friction-equivalent-1849--eve.date_basis: Paper dated 4 June, received 6 June, read 21 June 1849; 1850 is its journal publication year.
mech-joule-friction-equivalent-1849--eve.statement: Water, mercury and cast-iron friction series compared expended mechanical work with corrected heating. Joule preferred the water result 772.692 foot-pounds and rounded his conclusion to 772 per pound of water warmed by 1 °F near 55–60 °F.

mech-joule-magnetocalorimeter-1843--even.date_basis: The paper is signed July 1843 and was read at Cork on 21 August 1843; dates the reported apparatus, not an independently established construction day.
mech-joule-magnetocalorimeter-1843--even.statement: Joule rotated a compound electromagnet immersed in water between magnetic poles, measured circuit current with a galvanometer, and measured water-temperature change; the initial inducing magnets were reused from an electromagnetic engine.

mech-joule-series-two-apparatus-1843--ex.date_basis: The 1843 report distinguishes the new inducing magnet before series 2 and its later repeated use with weights; no exact trial day is assigned.
mech-joule-series-two-apparatus-1843--ex.statement: Joule reused the immersed rotating electromagnet with a newly built stationary inducing magnet in the later series 2 arrangement, then repeated that series with falling weights when estimating the 1843 heat equivalent.

mech-papplewick-drawing-1785--event-01.date_basis: Repository dates the surviving elevation to 1785; this is not used as a precise commissioning date.
mech-papplewick-drawing-1785--event-01.statement: Boulton & Watt elevation of the Robinson cotton mill showing an 11-horsepower sun-and-planet engine with 17½-inch cylinder and four-foot stroke, alongside evidence of the earlier waterwheel.

mech-regnault-steam-data-1847--event-01.date_basis: First published volume of the government-commissioned Relation des expériences, as identified contemporaneously by Thomson. Individual measurement dates are not assigned.
mech-regnault-steam-data-1847--event-01.statement: Published measurements of saturated-steam pressure and latent heat per unit mass, undertaken for steam-engine calculations; Thomson describes the published range as 0–230 °C and the missing density information needed for his calculations.

mech-rotative-specification-1781--event-.date_basis: Patent granted 25 October 1781; detailed specification signed 13 February and enrolled 23 February 1782.
mech-rotative-specification-1781--event-.statement: Watt's fifth patented method converts reciprocating engine motion into continuous shaft rotation with sun-and-planet gearing; the specification also describes an internal-tooth variant.

mech-rumford-friction-apparatus-1798--ev.date_basis: Dates the experimental report read 25 January 1798, not the construction or first observation. Exact experiment dates are not established here.
mech-rumford-friction-apparatus-1798--ev.statement: Rumford adapted a brass cannon end into a hollow cylinder, rotated by horse-driven boring machinery against a blunt tool; a thermometer and surrounding water registered frictional heating.

mech-soho-engine-shop-power-1783--event-.date_basis: Conversion occurred after the engine's 1783 corn-mill use and before its dismantling in 1803. Anchor 1793 is the interval midpoint for layout, not a claimed conversion year.
mech-soho-engine-shop-power-1783--event-.statement: The same Soho double-reciprocating engine was subsequently applied to lathes and drills in the engine shops; Southern called it the boring engine.

mech-soho-rotative-engine-1783--event-01.date_basis: First drawing dated August 1782; operation appears in a March 1783 diary reference, while the engine list gives first trial in June 1783.
mech-soho-rotative-engine-1783--event-01.statement: An 18-inch-cylinder, double-acting rotative engine using rack-and-sector connection and internal sun-and-planet gear, initially driving a corn mill.

mech-soho-trial-1775--event-01.date_basis: Trials reported in connection with the April 1775 replacement-cylinder correspondence and subsequent commercial supply.
mech-soho-trial-1775--event-01.statement: Watt's relocated experimental engine, rebuilt with Wilkinson's replacement cylinder and smaller parts made by Soho craftsmen, underwent promising trials.

mech-thomson-absolute-scale-1848--event-.date_basis: October 1848 Philosophical Magazine, vol. 33, pp. 313–317. This dates the published proposal.
mech-thomson-absolute-scale-1848--event-.statement: A thermometric scale in which a unit of heat descending through any one degree yields the same mechanical effect, constructed from Carnot-style reasoning and an approximate use of Regnault’s steam data.

mech-thomson-carnot-account-1849--append.date_basis: The appendix has its own explicit read date, separately from 2 January.
mech-thomson-carnot-account-1849--append.statement: Thomson compared Regnault-derived numerical heat-engine values with Carnot’s and Clapeyron’s earlier values in a separately read appendix.

mech-thomson-carnot-account-1849--event-.date_basis: Explicit read date printed with the original account; distinct from the later appendix.
mech-thomson-carnot-account-1849--event-.statement: Thomson presented an account using Regnault’s steam observations and discussing Joule while provisionally retaining caloric conservation.

mech-thomson-dynamical-heat-1851--event-.date_basis: Read 17 March 1851; original Transactions volume is dated 1853, and a Philosophical Magazine reprint appeared in 1852. This node dates the presentation.
mech-thomson-dynamical-heat-1851--event-.statement: Thomson explicitly combined Joule’s equivalence principle, reversible-engine reasoning attributed to Carnot and Clausius, and Regnault-based numerical results to construct a dynamical account of heat-engine performance.

mech-wilkinson-cylinder-1775--event-01.date_basis: The cylinder was ordered before the end of 1774 and Boulton reported its supply in a letter dated 24 April 1775. This establishes production by that letter, not production during 1775; no earlier production bound is established.
mech-wilkinson-cylinder-1775--event-01.statement: An approximately 18-inch replacement cylinder machined by John Wilkinson and supplied for Watt's experimental engine at Soho.

micrologic-f-commercial-1961.date_basis: Introduced in March and contemporary 29/31 March reports identify paid evaluation sales and an offer.
micrologic-f-commercial-1961.statement: The Micrologic flip-flop was being sold in evaluation quantities in March 1961; the introductory unit price was $120.

micrologic-prototype-1960.date_basis: Jay Last reports first working physically isolated Micrologic devices in May.
micrologic-prototype-1960.statement: The team made working physically isolated Micrologic flip-flop devices.

nonmarket-ra-i-1969--abandonment-1969.date_basis: A contemporary Reuters report puts initial evacuation on Wednesday 16 July while a return was contemplated; by the 22 July datelined interview Ra was reported left behind.
nonmarket-ra-i-1969--abandonment-1969.statement: The crew left the damaged Ra at sea and reached Barbados aboard Shenandoah; the 1969 voyage in Ra was abandoned.

nonmarket-ra-i-1969--practical-1969.date_basis: The 22 July 1969 participant interview reports departure from Safi on May 25.
nonmarket-ra-i-1969--practical-1969.statement: Ra departed Safi on the expedition’s experimental Atlantic voyage.

nonmarket-ra-i-1969--production-1969.date_basis: The museum dates construction of this vessel to 1969.
nonmarket-ra-i-1969--production-1969.statement: The papyrus vessel Ra was built in 1969 for the expedition.

zeiss-1-18-offer-1885.date_basis: Dated manufacturer catalogue describes prices and stock, but not its earliest offer.
zeiss-1-18-offer-1885.statement: Zeiss listed the 1/18 homogeneous-immersion objective at 400 marks without a correction mount and described the series as stocked in fixed mounts.

zeiss-1-18-withdrawal-by-1889.date_basis: The first catalogue still offers the part; the later one says it is no longer supplied.
zeiss-1-18-withdrawal-by-1889.statement: By its 1889 catalogue, Zeiss said it no longer supplied the former 1/18 homogeneous-immersion objective.
